corrections.text: This article quotes VentureBeat as saying 633 malicious npm packages passed verification "after attackers generated valid signing certificates from compromised maintainer accounts" and that Sigstore "could not determine whether credential holders authorized the publish." VentureBeat's original text uses the singular throughout: "the attacker had generated valid signing certificates from a compromised maintainer account" and "the person holding the credentials." The May 19 incident involved a single compromised maintainer account, not multiple, as this article's own later paragraph correctly states.

This article states that the May 19 npm incident and the November 9 bee-js/Swarm Desktop incident, discussed in this piece, are "eight months apart." The actual gap between May 19 and November 9 is approximately 5.7 months (about six months), not eight.
